confirmed.title: Two 404 requests for literal template strings on every load
confirmed.detail: The browser requests /{{ p.img }} and /{{ v.icon }} before the runtime processes the <sc-for> template. Harmless visually but two failed requests and two console errors per page view.
corrections: The requests come from the parser creating the raw elements (x-dc is only hidden with display:none), not solely the preload scanner; effect is identical.

Attribute it to the browser parsing the raw template's inside before the runtime replaces it, i.e. an artifact of the Claude Design runtime, not of the page authoring. It is harmless and disappears once the markup is ported, so it is a note rather than something to fix in the prototype (low, not medium).

confirmed.title: Page depends on the unpkg CDN at runtime
confirmed.detail: React and ReactDOM are loaded from unpkg when the page loads; without network the product grid and value tiles never render.
corrections: The dependency is stronger than stated: hideRawTemplate() (line 1820) injects x-dc{display:none!important} synchronously and init()/boot() run only after loadReactUmd() resolves (lines 1906-1910, failure logs and throws), so without network the ENTIRE page stays blank, not just the product grid and value tiles.

The consequence is understated. hideRawTemplate() (line 1818-1822, called unconditionally at 1906) injects 'x-dc{display:none!important}' before React is requested (confirmed live: that style is in <head>), and boot() never runs if the CDN fails, so without network the ENTIRE page stays blank, not just the product grid and value tiles. Severity should be raised accordingly.

The consequence is understated. hideRawTemplate() injects x-dc{display:none} immediately and loadReactUmd().then(init).catch() only logs and rethrows, so if unpkg is unreachable the entire page stays blank, not just the product grid and value tiles.

confirmed.title: Hero fade is offset by the nav height below 900px: black band across the photo plus a hard bottom edge
confirmed.detail: Under the max-width:900px media query the nav becomes position:relative with order:-2, so it is the first in-flow child of the hero section (88px tall at 375 and 768). The fade overlay keeps `top:0; height:max(62vw,320px)` positioned against the SECTION, not the image, so its gradient runs over the nav and the top of the photo and reaches solid #0d0c0a 88px above the photo's bottom. Result at every width under 900: the photo goes fully black in a horizontal band (through the man's hoodie/hands), then snaps back to full brightness for its last 88px, and ends with a hard edge against the black copy block. The story section does not have this problem because it has no in-flow element before the image (storyFade 2724-3004 == storyImg). Fix: offset the fade by the nav height, or wrap image+fade in one relative container so the fade tracks the image.

Under 520px the bar gets its own override of `padding:10px 16px`, which is a third gutter value (16px) rather than the 24px used elsewhere.
confirmed.evidence: Tablet 768 live DOM: announce paddingLeft 48px, nav paddingLeft 24px, hero-copy paddingLeft 24px. tablet-768.png top-left crop: announcement text begins x~48, logo at x~35, 'STREETWEAR WITH A PURPOSE' at x=24. HTML: `[data-r=pad]{padding-left:24px!important;padding-right:24px!important}` with zero data-r="pad" elements in the source; `[data-r=announce]{...padding:10px 16px!important}` only in the 520 query.

confirmed.title: Hero image band is sized with 62vw and no viewport-height cap: taller than the screen on landscape phones
confirmed.detail: `height:62vw` grows with width but is never limited by height. On an 812x375 landscape phone the band is 503px tall, 1.34x the viewport, and follows a 41px announcement bar and 88px nav, so the photo spans y=129-632 and the H1 starts at y=689, nearly two screens down; the fade offset from RESPONSIVE-1 also lands in the middle of that band. A `max-height` in vh (or clamp) on [data-r=hero-img]/[data-r=hero-fade] would keep the headline reachable in landscape.
confirmed.evidence: Live DOM at 812x375: heroImg y=129 h=503 w=797; heroFade y=41 h=503; h1 y=689 h=61; vh=375; docH 3939. CSS: `[data-r=hero-img]{...height:62vw!important;min-height:320px!important;order:-1}` inside the max-width:900px query, no max-height anywhere.

confirmed.title: Phone hero crop shows only the central two-thirds of the photo with no art direction; the third model and back-print message are cut
confirmed.detail: At 375 the band is 375x320 (aspect 1.17:1) filled from the 1672x941 (1.78:1) PNG with object-fit:cover. The cover scale is set by height (320/941 = 0.34), giving a 568px-wide scaled image of which 193px (34%) is cropped, 96px each side; `object-position:center 30%` has no effect because there is no vertical slack. The right-hand model with the 'Built Different For A Higher Purpose' back print (the only on-garment message in the hero) is cut through mid-body, and the group composition the mockup relies on becomes a two-person crop. No <picture>/srcset offers a portrait-oriented crop for phones (C10 covers weight; this is composition).
confirmed.evidence: Live DOM 375: heroImg 375x320; CSS `object-fit:cover;object-position:center 30%` inline, `object-position:center 30%!important` in the 900 query. Live 375 screenshot: third model visible only as a cap and sleeve at the right edge x~340-375, back print not visible. tablet-768.png (753x476 band, ~11% cropped) shows all three models and the back print. Arithmetic: 1672x941 scaled by 0.340 = 568x320; 568-375 = 193px cropped.
corrections: The visual consequence (third model cut mid-body, back print hidden) follows from the geometry and the group composition but could not be re-inspected in a true-375 capture here, since mobile-375.png is a wider layout; the crop arithmetic itself is correct.

confirmed.title: Footer stacks into a column at 521-900px although both groups fit on one row
confirmed.detail: The 900px query forces `flex-direction:column; align-items:flex-start` on the footer. At 768 the left group (logo + tagline) is 230px wide and the right group (two social icons + 'A Brighter Tomorrow') 271px wide, 501px in a 705px content box, so the row layout would still fit with the 32px gap. The stacked version makes a 164px-tall footer with the social icons left-aligned under the logo instead of the mockup's single band. Keeping the row down to ~560px and stacking only below that would match the desktop composition on tablets.
confirmed.evidence: Tablet 768 live DOM: footer y=3673 h=164, computed flexDirection 'column'; footerLeft x=24 w=230 y=3701; footerRight x=24 w=271 y=3781. CSS: `[data-r=footer]{flex-direction:column!important;align-items:flex-start!important;padding:28px 24px!important;gap:24px!important}` inside the max-width:900px query. Same 164px height at 375 (footer y=4218 h=164).
corrections: The stack at <=900 is an explicit authored breakpoint; this is a recommendation about where the breakpoint should sit, not a bug.

confirmed.title: 5.4-screen mobile page with a header that scrolls away and no back-to-top or persistent navigation
confirmed.detail: At 375x812 the document is 4,382px: hero 970 + New Drop 1,695 + Story 797 + Values 698 + Footer 164 (+59 announcement). The nav is `position:relative` below 900px, so even once the hamburger works (C5) the menu, search, account and cart are only reachable by scrolling back to the top; there is no sticky header, no back-to-top control and no in-footer links to the same destinations. On a long single-page store this is the main way phone users get to Shop/Cart.
confirmed.evidence: Live DOM 375x812: docH 4382, vh 812 (5.4 viewports); nav computed position 'relative', y=59 h=88; section heights hero 970, drop 1695, story 797, values 698, footer 164. Footer contains only two social links (footer a count = 2) and two taglines, no nav links. CSS: `[data-r=nav]{position:relative!important;padding:16px 24px!important;order:-2}`.

confirmed.title: Most mobile secondary text is 11-13px tracked uppercase; body copy never exceeds 15px
confirmed.detail: Apart from the H1 (56px), the H2s and the script, the phone typography is built from small tracked caps: 11px .22-.26em for the announcement bar, value subtitles (#bdb6a8 on #0d0c0a) and both footer taglines; 12px .2-.22em for product names, the story side caption, nav links and the two CTAs; 13px .3em for eyebrows; the only paragraph is 15px. Letter-spacing of .2-.3em at 11-13px on a 375px screen makes short labels long and light, and nothing on the page reaches the 16px commonly used as the mobile body floor. C16 already covers the 9px cart badge; this is the rest of the scale.
confirmed.evidence: Live DOM 375: computed font sizes on text leaves = 9, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 56px. HTML inline styles: announce `font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.22em`, value sub `font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.2em;color:#bdb6a8`, footer taglines `font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.26em`, product name `font-size:12px;letter-spacing:.2em`, CTAs `font-size:12px;letter-spacing:.22em`, story paragraph `font-size:15px`. No mobile override of any font size in the media queries except the clamp() minimums on headings.
corrections: The '16px' entry in the live list is the hidden <script type="text/x-dc"> node, not rendered text, so the statement that no visible text reaches 16px holds; the claim's own evidence line should not list 16px among text leaves.
The '16px' in the measured font-size list is the hidden <script type="text/x-dc"> element in <body> (it has a text node), not visible copy; the claim's 15px ceiling for readable text stands.
This scale reproduces the approved mockup's own small tracked caps, so it is a brand/mockup decision rather than an implementation slip, and the 16px 'floor' is a convention, not a requirement.

confirmed.title: Hero fade overlay is offset from the hero image by the nav height below 900px
confirmed.detail: Under 900px the nav becomes in-flow (`[data-r=nav]{position:relative;order:-2}`, line 29) and sits at the top of the hero grid, but `[data-r=hero-fade]{top:0;height:max(62vw,320px)}` (line 22) is still measured from the section top. The gradient therefore goes fully opaque 88px above the bottom of the photo, an unfaded strip of the photo reappears beneath the black band, and the image then ends in a hard edge against the copy. Fix by anchoring the fade to the image (wrap img+fade, or offset the fade by the nav height, or move the nav out of the hero section).
confirmed.evidence: Live DOM at 375x812: nav top 59 h 88 (position relative); hero-fade top 59 h 320 (y 59-379); hero-img top 147 h 320 (y 147-467); hero-copy starts at 467. Visible in mobile-375.png (top 640px): photo fades to solid black around y 300-380, then legs/steps reappear unfaded from ~380 to 467 with a hard cut. Same in tablet-768.png: fade reaches black at ~y 520, photo strip visible ~520-605, hard edge at 605. Story section is unaffected (story-img and story-fade both top 2724, h 280) because it has no in-flow element above the image.

confirmed.title: C4 is incorrect: the runtime implements style-hover, so both CTAs do have a hover state
confirmed.detail: support.js `collectProps` treats any `style-*` attribute as a pseudo-class (`if (key.startsWith("style-")) pseudoClasses.push(host.pseudoClass(key.slice(6), value))`) and `createPseudoSheet` inserts `.scpN:hover{...!important}` into a head stylesheet while adding the class to the element. The attribute is stripped from the DOM (which is why the earlier count was 0) but the effect is live, and the `!important` beats the inline background. C4 should be withdrawn. What remains true: `style-hover` is a Claude-Design-only attribute, so the hover must be re-expressed as ordinary CSS when the markup leaves the dc-runtime (e.g. for Shopify); the nav links' only hover is the global `a:hover{color:#d8c08a}` (line 16), and the PNG icon links have no hover at all.
confirmed.evidence: support.js lines ~424-427 (collectProps) and the createPseudoSheet block (~lines 1535-1560). Live head stylesheet rules: `.scp0:hover { background: rgb(42, 40, 35) !important; color: rgb(243, 239, 230) !important; }` and `.scp1:hover { background: rgb(230, 211, 166) !important; color: rgb(13, 12, 10) !important; }`; rendered anchors: `View All Products →`, `Our Story →`.

confirmed.title: Template syntax uses Liquid's own {{ }} delimiters, so a direct paste into a Shopify section silently renders empty product and value tiles
confirmed.detail: The product grid and value tiles are driven by `<sc-for list="{{ products }}">`, `<sc-if value="{{ p.img }}">`, `{{ p.name }}`, `{{ p.price }}`, `background:{{ s }}`, `{{ v.icon }}`, `{{ v.title }}`, `{{ v.sub }}` (lines 107-120, 143-149) and all data lives only in `<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script>` (lines 169-188), which nothing but support.js executes. Liquid evaluates `{{ products }}`/`{{ p.name }}` as undefined variables and outputs empty strings, and `<sc-for>`, `<sc-if>`, `<x-dc>`, `<helmet>` stay in the DOM as unknown elements. The grid must be rewritten as `{% for product in collection.products %}` with `product.featured_image | image_url`, `product.price | money`, etc., and the values block as section blocks with schema.
confirmed.evidence: HTML lines 9-10, 107-120, 143-149, 169-188; support.js `walkFor`/`walkIf`/`compileAttr` are the only consumers of that syntax; the two 404s for `/%7B%7B%20p.img%20%7D%7D` and `/%7B%7B%20v.icon%20%7D%7D` show the browser already treats the placeholders literally before the runtime runs.

confirmed.title: The commerce surface is inert: no product links, placeholder hrefs, hard-coded cart count and symbol-only currency
confirmed.detail: Nothing in the New Drop grid is clickable or focusable: the `[data-r=products]` container holds 0 `<a>` elements, product names are `<div>`s, and there is no add-to-cart. Six of the nine links are `href="#"` (Home, Verse, View All Products, Our Story CTA, Facebook, Instagram), which scroll to the top of the page when clicked; Shop and Collections both point at `#shop`; the Home active underline (line 71) is hard-coded. The cart badge is the literal text `0` (line 78). Prices are string-concatenated in JS (`cur + '1,290'`, lines 172-177) so the `currency` prop (data-props enum ₱/$/€) only swaps the symbol; selecting `$` shows `$1,290` for the same item. For Shopify these become `product.url`, `product.price | money`, `cart.item_count`, `routes.*`.
confirmed.evidence: Live DOM: productsAnchors 0, productsChildren 3; focusables = A:#:Home, A:#shop:Shop, A:#shop:Collections, A:#story:Our Story, A:#:Verse, A:#:View All Products, A:#:Our Story, A:#:Facebook, A:#:Instagram; cartBadge '0'. `grep -c 'href="#"'` = 6. HTML lines 71-72, 78, 104, 132, 160-161, 169-177.

confirmed.title: Colour swatches have no accessible name or semantics
confirmed.detail: Each swatch is `<span style="width:16px;height:16px;border-radius:50%;background:{{ s }}">` (line 116): no text, no title, no aria-label, no role, and the colour name is not stated anywhere on the page. Screen-reader users get nothing, and they are not interactive (no variant selection), so they also fail as controls. Either give each an sr-only label with the colour name (from `variant.option1` in Shopify) or mark the row `aria-hidden` and put the colour names in text.
confirmed.evidence: Live DOM: 9 swatch spans, each with aria-label null, title '', role null, textContent ''. Backgrounds rgb(13,12,10), rgb(243,239,230), rgb(75,84,67).

confirmed.title: Every icon is a ~30 KB RGBA PNG rendered at 16-44 px; ~350 KB of raster that cannot be recoloured
confirmed.detail: Ten icon placements come from nine 110-150 px PNGs totalling 308,521 bytes: icon-globe.png (35,625 B) is drawn at 16 px in the announcement bar and 44 px in the values row; search/account/cart (28-29 KB each) at 24 px; facebook/instagram (37-42 KB) at 28 px; crown/community/diamond (33-40 KB) at 44 px. The logo is a 500x500 PNG (37,836 B) drawn at 78/56 px. Because the colour is baked into the pixels, no CSS hover/focus colour is possible (the global `a:hover{color:#d8c08a}` does nothing for the social links) and the icons cannot follow theme colour settings. Inline SVG (or a single SVG sprite with `currentColor`) would be well under 1 KB each.
confirmed.evidence: File sizes from `stat` in images/; `file` reports 110x110 / 130x110 / 150x110 / 130x130 RGBA PNGs; live measurements: icon-globe 16x16 and 44x44, search/account/cart 24x24, facebook/instagram 28x28, crown 52x44, community 60x44, diamond 52x44, logo 56/78 px from naturalWidth 500. Referenced page weight 2,491,648 B across 17 files, of which icons+logo are 346 KB and hero-group.png is 1,989 KB.
corrections: 'Cannot be recoloured' is slightly absolute (CSS filters can tint a raster), but no clean hover/theme colouring is possible, so the point stands.

confirmed.title: support.js is an editor/streaming runtime: hidden-until-React render chain, double HTML fetch, new Function eval and editor bookkeeping in the DOM
confirmed.detail: (a) `hideRawTemplate()` injects `x-dc{display:none!important}` and `loadReactUmd()` then appends two unpkg scripts with `async=false`, so nothing is visible until HTML -> support.js -> React -> ReactDOM have all arrived and `boot()` has run (three dependent hops before first content). (b) `boot()` calls `fetch(location.href)` and recompiles/re-renders the whole template from the raw text, so the HTML document is requested twice and React renders the page twice on every load; on file:// this fetch simply fails. (c) The `<script data-dc-script>` logic is evaluated with `new Function` (`evalDcLogic`), which requires `unsafe-eval` under any CSP. (d) The rendered DOM carries 137 `data-dc-tpl` attributes and 14 `.sc-interp` wrapper spans (editor bookkeeping), and the runtime posts `__dc_booted`/`__dc_design_mode` messages to `window.parent` with origin `*`. None of this belongs in a production theme; the markup needs to be extracted as static Liquid/HTML with no dc-runtime.
confirmed.evidence: support.js: hideRawTemplate ~line 1818-1822; loadScript/loadReactUmd ~1823-1847 (`s.async = false`); boot() `fetch(location.href)` line 159 followed by `runtime.updateHtml(rootName, raw.template)`; `evalDcLogic` `new Function(...)` line 844 (and 1218 for x-import); postMessage at ~1385-1388 and ~1855-1862. Network log per load: `/God%20Squad%20Website.dc.html` appears twice (document + `fetch`), plus support.js, two unpkg scripts, Google Fonts CSS. Live DOM: dcTplAttrs 137, scInterp 14, head scripts = support.js, react.production.min.js, react-dom.production.min.js.

confirmed.title: Sections are not full-bleed above 1440px; the cream New Drop band and hero photo sit in a 1440px box with dark gutters
confirmed.detail: Everything is wrapped in `<div style="width:100%;max-width:1440px;margin:0 auto;background:#0d0c0a;overflow:hidden">` (line 55) and section backgrounds are on the inner sections, so on any viewport wider than 1440 the #f3efe6 New Drop section, the hero photograph and the value-row borders stop at the wrapper edge while body shows #0d0c0a either side. The renders were only captured up to 1440 so this was not visible. Fix: give each section a full-width background and constrain only an inner container.
confirmed.evidence: Live at 1920x1080: wrapper, #shop and hero-img all left 233 / right 1673 / width 1440; #shop background rgb(243,239,230), body background rgb(13,12,10); h1 at its 112px clamp cap.

confirmed.title: Font loading: preconnect is incomplete and the stylesheet link lives in the body template
confirmed.detail: Line 11 preconnects only to fonts.googleapis.com (the CSS host) and without `crossorigin`; the five font files come from fonts.gstatic.com, which has no preconnect, so each font-file fetch waits for a fresh DNS/TLS handshake after the CSS arrives. The `<link>`s sit inside `<helmet>` in the body: the runtime removes them with `<x-dc>` and re-appends clones to `<head>` during render (`createHelmetManager.compile`). In a Shopify theme these fonts should come from `font_picker` settings / `font_face` (or self-hosted assets/) rather than a Google Fonts `<link>`.
confirmed.evidence: HTML lines 11-12; live head: `preconnect https://fonts.googleapis.com/ co=null` is the only preconnect; support.js helmet compile (~lines 1420-1470) clones LINK/META nodes into head. document.fonts shows Jost 400/500/600, Kaushan Script 400 and Playfair Display 900 loaded from gstatic.

confirmed.title: Dead, duplicate and unsafe-named assets: 16.9 MB project for a 2.5 MB page, plus a no-op background colour on the logo wrappers
confirmed.detail: The page references 17 files (2,491,648 B) but the folder holds 16.9 MB. Byte-identical copies by md5: hero-group.png x3 (images/, root `chatgpt-image-sep-20-...png`, uploads/`ChatGPT Image ... 11_06_34 AM.png`), icons-sprite.png x3 (two uploads copies), social-sprite.png x2, logo.png = uploads/God-Squad-Images/06-logo.png, our-story.webp = 05-our-story-models.webp; the two 2172x724 sprites (834 KB + 928 KB) are unreferenced, as are `GODSQUAD WEBSITE MOCKUP.png` (1.87 MB), two different `white-font-trans-*.png` in the root and three pasted editor screenshots (3.9 MB). None of this should be copied into a theme's assets/. Separately, the logo wrappers use `background:#0230` (lines 69 and 155): a 4-digit hex whose alpha is 0, so it is dead CSS. The logo asset itself is `images/WHITE FONT LOGO.png` (spaces and uppercase, requested as `WHITE%20FONT%20LOGO.png`); rename it to a URL-safe asset name before it goes into assets/.
confirmed.evidence: `md5sum` output: c5f73461... for all three hero copies, e5f38184... for the three sprite copies, 59f7085f... for both social sprites, 01f17bc1... for logo.png/06-logo.png, 07accc16... for our-story.webp/05-our-story-models.webp; `du -sk .` = 16,890 KB; live computed background of the logo wrapper = rgba(0, 34, 51, 0); network request `/images/WHITE%20FONT%20LOGO.png`.

confirmed.title: Inline-style-only CSS with an !important attribute-selector responsive layer; header is structurally welded to the hero
confirmed.detail: There are 77 `style="` attributes and zero classes; the responsive behaviour is 55 `!important` declarations keyed on `[data-r=...]` attributes (lines 17-52, 60 data-r hooks in the file). Palette literals are repeated (#0d0c0a x18, #f3efe6 x13, #d8c08a x10) so nothing can be driven by theme settings. The `<nav>` is a child of the hero `<section>`, absolutely positioned over it, with the hero copy padded `170px` top (line 82) and `190px` (line 90) to clear it, and the announcement bar is a sibling div. In a Shopify 2.0 theme the announcement bar and header must be sections in the header group and the hero a separate section; as written the header cannot be separated from the hero without re-laying out the hero (and TECHNICAL-1 is a direct consequence of that coupling). Colours, fonts and copy need to move to `settings_schema.json`/section schema.
confirmed.evidence: grep counts on the HTML: `style="` 77, `!important` 55, `data-r=` 60, `class=` 0, `#0d0c0a` 18, `#f3efe6` 13, `#d8c08a` 10; HTML lines 17-52 (media rules), 64-95 (nav inside hero, hero-copy padding 170px, hero-side padding 190px), 58-61 (announcement bar).

refuted.title: CTA hover styles are dead
why: REFUTE: The runtime does implement style-hover. support.js collectProps (lines 428-429) converts any style-* attribute into host.pseudoClass(...); createPseudoSheet (lines 1567-1590) inserts '.scpN:hover{...}' with importantify() into a head stylesheet and the class is added to the element (lines 809-811). Live DOM: rules '.scp0:hover { background: rgb(42, 40, 35) !important; color: rgb(243, 239, 230) !important; }' and '.scp1:hover { background: rgb(230, 211, 166) !important; ... }' exist and the two CTAs carry class scp0/scp1. The attribute count of 0 only reflects that the attribute is consumed, not that the hover is dead. | correction: Both CTAs have a working hover state under the dc-runtime. The real finding is that style-hover is a Claude-Design-only convention that must be re-expressed as ordinary CSS when the markup leaves support.js (as TECHNICAL-2 states).

refuted.title: Desktop render is faithful to the approved mockup
why: REFUTE: The 1440 render departs from the mockup in more than C1, C14 and sharpness: the hero photo is a three-model group (mockup: single capped model), the headline breaks WALK/BY/FAITH. on three lines (mockup: two), the nav wordmark is 66x50 versus the mockup's 114x87 on a narrower canvas, the story heading breaks on three lines (mockup: two), products sit in visible cream tiles with the cap edge-cropped, the social icons are circled, and the globe is gold. Palette, copy, section order and type families do match, but the composition claim for the hero is not accurate. | correction: Restate as: palette, copy, section order and typefaces match the mockup at 1440; composition differs in the hero photo, headline and story-heading line breaks, wordmark size, product tiles, social icon style and globe colour (see FIDELITY-1 through FIDELITY-9).

critic_additions.title: Three of five nav links fail contrast over the hero sky at 1024 and 1440 (Collections, Our Story, Verse at 2.4-2.9:1)
critic_additions.detail: The primary navigation is 12px white text laid directly on the hero photo. Home and Shop land on the left model's dark hair and pass easily, but Collections, Our Story and Verse sit on the bright sky and tower between the two models, where the vertical fade has already thinned to about 0.4 alpha. Effective contrast is 2.4-2.9:1 (WCAG AA needs 4.5:1 for this size). At 1024 the gold Home link also moves onto a bright area and drops to 3.5:1. The search/account/cart icons at 1440 sit at 3.7-4.8:1, just above the 3:1 UI-component floor. In the approved mockup the nav sits on a dark building top, so this is a consequence of the hero photo swap (FIDELITY-1) plus a top fade that is too weak (.55 at 0% to 0 at 30%). A solid or stronger top band under the nav, or moving the nav out of the hero (TECHNICAL-11), fixes it without touching the photo.
critic_additions.evidence: Measured in the Browser pane at 1440x900 and 1024x900: the same-origin images/hero-group.png was drawn to a canvas with the rendered cover crop, photo luminance averaged under each element's box, then composited with the inline gradient alphas at the element centre (hero-fade, line 66: horizontal stops .92/.75/.15/.1/.8, vertical .55 at 0% to 0 at 30%; nav text baseline y=91-103 gives aV about 0.39-0.41). Contrast of #f3efe6 (or #d8c08a for Home) against the effective background, 1440: Home 7.4:1, Shop 7.8:1, Collections 2.8:1 (photo L=.55, aH=.17), Our Story 2.4:1 (L=.62, aH=.13), Verse 2.4:1 (L=.63, aH=.11); Search 3.7:1, Account 4.1:1, Cart 4.8:1. 1024: Home (gold) 3.5:1 (L=.74), Shop 10:1, Collections 2.9:1, Our Story 2.4:1, Verse 2.4:1, Cart 4.6:1. Visible in desktop-1440.png at x=619-947, y=91 and laptop-1024.png at x=411-739, y=91, where the three links overlay the sky and tower. Mockup 00-full-mockup-reference.webp: nav links at y=87 over a dark facade.

critic_additions.title: C13 understates the failure mode: if React cannot be fetched the whole page is blank, not just the grid and tiles (file:// itself is fine)
critic_additions.detail: support.js hides the entire <x-dc> template synchronously at parse time and only reveals it by mounting React. The React/ReactDOM load from unpkg has no fallback: on failure the catch logs one console error and re-throws, and the hiding style is never removed, so an ad-blocker, corporate proxy, captive portal, offline demo or SRI mismatch produces a completely black page with no message. Everything visible (announcement bar, hero, nav, footer) is inside <x-dc>, so nothing survives. Separately, opening the file by double-click (file://) does work: boot() parses the template from the live DOM first and the self-fetch that fails on file:// is only a refresh with an empty catch. With JavaScript disabled the raw template shows instead, including a product card that reads '{{ p.name }}' with a broken '{{ p.img }}' image.
critic_additions.evidence: support.js 1818-1822: hideRawTemplate() appends 'x-dc{display:none!important}' to <head>; called at line 1906 before loadReactUmd(). Lines 1907-1910: loadReactUmd().then(init).catch((err) => { console.error('[dc] failed to load React or boot:', err); throw err; }) with no un-hide or fallback render. Lines 1143-1146: React/ReactDOM 18.3.1 production UMD from unpkg with SRI. All page markup is inside <x-dc> (dc.html lines 9-168). boot() lines 150-164: parseDcDocument(doc) runs first; fetch(location.href) at 159 has .catch(() => {}). <helmet> style/link (lines 10-54) are in the body, so the no-JS raw view is styled.

critic_additions.title: The peso sign in every price and the arrow in both CTAs are not in Jost and render in the system fallback font
critic_additions.detail: Jost's loaded faces do not contain U+20B1 (₱) or U+2192 (→). The browser substitutes a per-character system fallback, so the currency symbol next to Jost 600 digits and the arrow next to Jost 500 button text come from a different typeface (on this Windows machine the width matches the generic serif, i.e. Times New Roman, with synthesized weight). The result differs per OS (Segoe/Times on Windows, Helvetica/SF on macOS and iOS, Roboto on Android), so prices and CTAs will not look the same across devices, and none match the mockup, whose ₱ is a sans glyph matching the digits. Fix: use an SVG or icon arrow, and either pick a font that includes ₱ for the price element, add a small subset font for the symbol, or render the currency as 'PHP'.
critic_additions.evidence: Measured in the Browser pane with hidden spans. '₱' at font:600 14px: 8.56px with 'Jost', 8.56px with 'Jost, serif', 8.56px with 'serif', but 7.70px with 'Jost, monospace' and 7.70px with 'monospace'. critic_additions.title: The Our Story slot needs an image at least 2000 px wide; both the current crop and the unused replacement are far too small, so C1's asset swap alone still yields a soft image
critic_additions.detail: C1 correctly identifies the wrong asset, but the fix it implies (use images/our-story.webp) does not solve the resolution problem. The section renders the image at about 1000 CSS px wide on desktop, and both candidate files are small lossy crops of the 1024x1536 mockup. The current file is already upscaled 1.5x on a 1x display and about 3x on a 2x display, and the three-model crop would be upscaled even more. On top of that, object-position:center top with cover scaling discards 29% of the picture's height at 1440 (the hands and chest), so what is shown is a cropped fragment of an upscaled fragment. The section needs an original photograph (or a re-render) at roughly 2000 px wide with a srcset, not another mockup crop.
critic_additions.evidence: 01-hero-model-mu98p88t-7jig.webp is 650x480 (39,966 B), rendered at 998x520 CSS px at 1440 (scale 1.535; 1,996 device px on a 2x screen, 3.07x), 753x461 at 768 and 375x280 at 375. Cover math at 1440: scaled 998x737, 217 px (29%) of height cut from the bottom because of object-position:center top (line 126). images/our-story.webp (C1's replacement) is 535x348 (41,004 B): 1.87x at 1440, 3.7x on 2x. Both are described in uploads/God-Squad-Images README as crops from the 1024x1536 mockup, so no larger master exists in the project.

critic_additions.title: Hero PNG has no alpha channel, so the PNG format buys nothing; it is a straight JPEG/WebP conversion
critic_additions.detail: C10 gives the weight of the hero image but not why it is that large: the file is a photographic RGB PNG. There is no transparency to preserve, so it can be re-encoded as JPEG or WebP without any compositing changes and would typically shrink by roughly an order of magnitude at the same visual quality. The logo is the only asset that actually needs an alpha channel.
critic_additions.evidence: PNG IHDR read from disk: images/hero-group.png = 1672x941, bit depth 8, colour type 2 (RGB, no alpha), 1,989,201 bytes. images/WHITE FONT LOGO.png = 500x500, colour type 6 (RGBA). The three product images are already WebP (9-12 KB each).

critic_additions.title: No favicon, meta description, canonical or Open Graph/Twitter tags
critic_additions.detail: Beyond the empty title and missing lang (C7), the document head carries no favicon link, no description, no canonical URL and no social preview tags. Shared as-is, the URL produces a link card with no title, no description and no image, and the browser tab shows the default document icon. For the Shopify port these come from the theme's head snippet, but the prototype gives the port nothing to carry over (no chosen description copy, no OG image).
critic_additions.evidence: dc.html lines 3-7: <head> contains only <meta charset>, <meta viewport> and <script src="./support.js">. grep -i for favicon, rel="icon", og:, description, canonical across the .dc.html and support.js returns nothing. The runtime's helmet manager only re-appends the Google Fonts <link> and the <style> (lines 10-54).

critic_additions.title: Footer has no copyright, policy, contact or navigation links (mockup omits them too; open decision)
critic_additions.detail: The footer is purely decorative: logo, tagline, two social links to '#' and the 'A Brighter Tomorrow' line. There is no copyright line, no privacy/terms/shipping/returns link, no contact or newsletter capture, and no repeat of Shop / Our Story for users who reach the bottom of a 4,400 px mobile page (RESPONSIVE-10). The approved mockup shows the same minimal band, so this is a content decision to make before the Shopify port rather than a build defect, but a store footer normally carries the legal links.
critic_additions.evidence: dc.html lines 153-166: <footer> contains the logo div, 'Different People. Same Purpose.', two <a href="#"> social links, a divider and 'A Brighter Tomorrow'; no other links or text. Mockup 00-full-mockup-reference.webp bottom band (y=1420-1520 of 1536) shows the same elements plus TikTok/YouTube (C14).

critic_additions.title: Product names and value titles are plain divs, CTA arrows are unlabelled glyphs, and the hamburger's aria-label sits on a role-less span
critic_additions.detail: The document outline is h1 'Walk By Faith.' then h2 'The Faithful' and h2 'Real People. Bigger Purpose.' with nothing beneath the product or value groups, so heading navigation cannot reach a product. Both CTAs include a bare arrow span that screen readers append as 'rightwards arrow' to the link name. The hamburger's aria-label is on a <span> with no role, which ARIA 1.2 prohibits on generic elements and which most screen readers ignore, so even when C5/C6 are fixed the label needs a real button.

gaps: Keyboard walkthrough: Tab order through the 9 links, visibility of the default focus ring on the dark photo and on the cream section, Enter/Space on each control, and the absence of a skip link. Only the DOM inventory was checked, not actual keyboard use.

Screen-reader pass (NVDA/JAWS on Windows, VoiceOver on macOS/iOS) to hear how the ₱ and → fallbacks, the div-based product names, the image alt text (story alt says 'community' but shows one man), and the role-less hamburger are announced.

Lighthouse and axe-core runs. The contrast figures above are computed from sampled photo luminance and gradient alphas, not from an accessibility engine; an axe run would also catch anything the manual pass missed, and Lighthouse would give throttled LCP/FCP/CLS for the three-hop runtime chain and the 2 MB PNG. My buffered CLS read was 0 on a warm localhost load and LCP did not report, so no performance numbers exist yet.

Cold-cache, throttled (Slow 4G, 4x CPU) load to see how long the page stays blank while support.js, React, ReactDOM and the second HTML fetch arrive, and whether the display=swap fonts cause a visible Playfair/Georgia reflow of the headline.

Empirical test of the failure modes derived from code: block unpkg.com in DevTools (expected: black page, one console error), disable JavaScript (expected: raw template with '{{ p.name }}'), and open the file by double-click from OneDrive. The Browser pane served the file over its own HTTP server, so true file:// was not exercised.

Genuine 375px and landscape 812x375 device captures (RESPONSIVE-2/7); the mobile-375.png is a clipped ~490px layout and stops inside the values strip, so the fourth value tile and the footer were never seen at phone size. Test on a real iPhone (Safari) and Android Chrome, including text-wrap:balance support in older Safari.

Widths that were not captured: 1920/2560 (TECHNICAL-8's dark gutters are asserted from the wrapper CSS), the 901-1023 band (measured at 920: h1 78px, 'FAITH.' 264px wide overflows its 247px content box by 17px into the padding, harmless but unseen), and the 521-767 band (measured: the headline stays on one line at 56px down to at least 560px, products 2-up at 286px at 640; the two-line lockup only appears below roughly 540px, which refines FIDELITY-2).

Cross-browser renders in Firefox and Safari (aspect-ratio tiles, !important object-position overrides, Kaushan Script rotation, font smoothing) and Windows High Contrast / forced-colors mode, where the gold-on-black palette and raster PNG icons behave differently from CSS-coloured SVG.

Hover and focus-state pass with screenshots: nav a:hover to gold (Home is already gold so it has no hover change), the two style-hover CTAs, and the social icon links that have no hover at all; TECHNICAL-2 is code-derived, not observed.
